questions.question: When should you increase the distance between your vehicle and the vehicle ahead?

options.text: When you are following a small passenger vehicle.
When another driver is tailgating you.
When you are driving slower than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: When another driver is tailgating you.
questions.explanation: When being tailgated, create extra space in front of your vehicle. Do not brake suddenly. Slow down gradually or change lanes to prevent a collision.

questions.question: Alcohol is:

options.text: A stimulant.
A depressant.
Neither of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: A depressant.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows your nerves and body functions. It reduces your inhibitions and makes it harder to concentrate and stay alert.

questions.question: Two sets of solid double yellow lines that are two or more feet apart:

options.text: May be crossed to enter or exit a private driveway.
May not be crossed for any reason.
Should be treated as a separate traffic lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: May not be crossed for any reason.
questions.explanation: Two sets of solid double yellow lines spaced two or more feet apart form a barrier. Do not drive over this barrier or turn across it, except at designated openings.

questions.question: Your vehicle's wheels run off the edge of the pavement. What should you do first?

options.text: Turn the steering wheel slightly left to edge back onto the pavement.
Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas pedal, and gently apply the brakes.
Apply the brakes and turn the steering wheel sharply to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas pedal, and gently apply the brakes.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas pedal, and gently apply the brakes. Once your speed has reduced, check the traffic and safely return to the roadway. Do not jerk the wheel sharply, as this can cause you to lose control or enter another lane.

questions.question: When can you legally turn left at a red traffic light after stopping?

options.text: When you are on a two-way street and turning onto a two-way street.
When you are on a one-way street and turning onto another one-way street.
When you yield to all other traffic at the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are on a one-way street and turning onto another one-way street.
questions.explanation: After stopping completely, you may turn left at a red light only if you are on a one-way street and turning onto another one-way street. Check for posted signs that may prohibit this turn.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slippery when wet.
Stop sign ahead.
No U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of wet road conditions that can cause you to lose control. Slow down when you see wet pavement because it takes longer to stop.

questions.question: In bad weather, you should:

options.text: Steer off the road.
Drive in a low gear.
Steer and brake smoothly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer and brake smoothly.
questions.explanation: Do not slam on the brakes or make sharp turns in bad weather. These actions make it harder to control your vehicle.

questions.question: If you have a sudden tire blowout, you should:

options.text: Use the brakes lightly.
Pump the brakes.
Apply the brakes firmly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the brakes lightly.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel tightly and keep the vehicle straight. Slow down gradually by releasing the gas pedal and using light brake pressure.

questions.question: What is the benefit of keeping space around your vehicle?

options.text: Other drivers can cut in front of you, improving traffic flow.
You have time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
It inflates to protect you from injury in a collision.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
questions.explanation: Space around your vehicle gives you time to safely react. For example, extra space may give you time to brake or move out of the way if a vehicle enters your lane.

questions.question: When planning to pass another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Not assume the other driver will make room for you to return to your lane.
Assume the other driver will let you pass if you signal.
Assume the other driver will maintain the same speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not assume the other driver will make room for you to return to your lane.
questions.explanation: Even when you signal, do not assume the space is free or that other drivers will give you the right-of-way.

questions.question: Alcohol is:

options.text: A stimulant.
An antihistamine.
A depressant.

questions.correctAnswerText: A depressant.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It dulls your judgment and makes your reflexes slow.

questions.question: You should always drive:

options.text: At the speed of the vehicles around you.
At the speed limit.
At a speed that fits the road and weather conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: At a speed that fits the road and weather conditions.
questions.explanation: Your driving speed should match road conditions, weather, and the legal speed limit. Never exceed the speed limit. Slow down when conditions are less than ideal.

questions.question: When driving at night, you should:

options.text: Always use your high beams.
Look directly at the headlights of oncoming vehicles.
Increase your following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous because visibility is low. This makes it hard to judge speed and distance. Increase your following distance to help prevent a collision if the vehicle in front stops suddenly. Use your headlights properly and follow high beam and low beam rules.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Rely on the rearview mirror.
Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.
Rely on the left side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.
questions.explanation: Glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes. Look several times if needed. Watch both the traffic ahead and the traffic in the next lane.

questions.question: If your wheels drop off the roadway edge, you should:

options.text: Wait until it is safe, then gradually return to the roadway.
Turn back onto the roadway immediately.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until it is safe, then gradually return to the roadway.
questions.explanation: Do not turn back immediately. Reduce your speed, check the traffic, and gradually turn back onto the roadway when it is safe.

questions.question: You hit a parked car in a minor collision and cannot find the owner. What must you do?

options.text: Leave a note on the vehicle.
Report the collision right away to the local police or, in unincorporated areas, to the California Highway Patrol.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: If you hit a parked car or property, you must leave a note with your name, phone number, and address attached to the vehicle. You must also report the collision to the local city police or, in unincorporated areas, to the California Highway Patrol.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield sign.
School crossing sign.
Stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield sign.
questions.explanation: A triangle-shaped sign pointing downward is always a yield sign. You must be ready to slow down or stop when you see a yield sign.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You are traveling in the wrong direction.
Treat the intersection like a stop sign.
Do not proceed until the light turns green.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat the intersection like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. Come to a complete stop at the stop line or before the crosswalk. Yield to all other traffic and pedestrians before entering the intersection.

questions.question: Which vehicles must always stop before crossing railroad tracks?

options.text: Tank trucks marked with hazardous materials placards.
Motor homes or pickup trucks towing a boat trailer.
Any vehicle with three or more axles weighing more than 4,000 pounds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tank trucks marked with hazardous materials placards.
questions.explanation: Trucks carrying hazardous materials must stop before crossing railroad tracks.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Road construction or maintenance area ahead.
Side road ahead.
Railroad ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road construction or maintenance area ahead.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs warn of hazards ahead. Orange color means there is construction or maintenance work on the road.

questions.question: What color are regulatory signs?

options.text: Green.
Yellow.
White.

questions.correctAnswerText: White.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs tell drivers what laws they must follow. These signs are usually white squares or rectangles with black, red, or green text or symbols.

questions.question: Your license can be suspended if you are under 21 and drive with what blood alcohol level?

options.text: 0.15 percent or higher.
0.08 percent or higher.
Any amount.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any amount.
questions.explanation: Anyone under 21 cannot drive with any amount of alcohol. Any trace of alcohol in your system will result in penalties, including a two-year license suspension.

questions.question: When you merge onto the freeway, what speed should you drive?

options.text: At or near the speed of the freeway traffic.
At the legal speed limit.
Slower than the freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: At or near the speed of the freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: Enter the freeway at or near the speed of traffic, unless traffic is going faster than the legal speed limit.

questions.question: Cars are passing you on both sides while you drive in the center lane of an expressway. What should you do?

options.text: Stay in the center lane.
Move to the right lane.
Move to the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right lane.
questions.explanation: On roads with four or more lanes, drive in the right lanes unless you are passing or turning left. If you are driving below traffic speed on an interstate highway, use the right lane.

questions.question: What does a yellow left turn arrow mean?

options.text: Get ready to yield to oncoming traffic.
The protected left turn is ending soon.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: A yellow left arrow means the protected turn is ending. You must be ready to yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings, what should you always do?

options.text: Stop, listen, and go slowly.
Look left and right to see what is coming.
Slowly pass vehicles that appear to be stopped for no reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look left and right to see what is coming.
questions.explanation: At places where traffic crosses or pedestrians may enter, look to your left and right to make sure nothing is coming toward you.

questions.question: When traffic is moving at 50 to 55 mph, you will have the fewest accidents if you:

options.text: Drive a few miles per hour faster than other vehicles.
Stay within that speed range.
Drive a few miles per hour slower than other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay within that speed range.
questions.explanation: Drive at the same speed as other traffic (within posted speed limits). Vehicles moving at the same speed cannot hit each other. Accidents happen when vehicles drive at different speeds.

questions.question: A large truck ahead is turning right onto a street with two lanes in each direction. What will it do?

options.text: It may complete the turn in either lane.
It may have to swing wide to complete the right turn.
It must stay in the right lane while turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: It may have to swing wide to complete the right turn.
questions.explanation: When turning, the rear wheels follow a shorter path than the front wheels. Long trucks need extra space to turn right, so they may swing wide.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: Treat it like a stop sign.
Stop and yield to all cross traffic.
Slow down and stay alert.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stay alert.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means proceed with caution. Slow down and be alert. Yield to pedestrians, bicycles, and vehicles in the intersection, but you do not have to stop.

questions.question: Large trucks are likely to lose speed when:

options.text: Driving up long or steep hills.
Driving in long, gentle curves.
Driving down long, gentle hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving up long or steep hills.
questions.explanation: Large trucks slow down going uphill because they take longer to accelerate than smaller vehicles. Give trucks extra space when you drive behind them, especially on hills.
